title: The Palm Tree of Deborah (Tomer Devorah)
author: Moses Cordovero (Nataf trans)
description: Tomer Devorah (The Palm Tree of Deborah) by Rabbi Moses Cordovero (the Ramak, 1522-1570), here in an English translation (the index credits Nataf). A short classic of Kabbalistic ethics written in Safed, it opens with the principle that a person should resemble the Creator, being configured 'in the secret of the Highest Form' in both image and likeness. The first chapter expounds the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy from Micah 7:18-20 as patterns for human conduct: patience, forgiveness, bearing insult, and loving even those who wrong us. Following chapters show how to imitate each of the ten sefirot, from the humility of Keter and the wisdom of Chokhmah through the kindness of Chesed, the restraint of Gevurah and the beauty of Tiferet, to the receptive Malkhut, in daily behaviour, thought and speech. It is one of the most influential works of Jewish musar and mystical ethics, translating sefirotic theory into practice.
